clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11054 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry". This order (27 FR 9695, Federal Register of October 2, 1962, signed October 1, 1962) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members to inquire into the issues in labor disputes between maritime-industry employers (steamship companies, operators or agents of ships serving Atlantic and Gulf Coast ports from Searsport, Maine, to Brownsville, Texas, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, lighterage operators and other employers in related pier activities) and certain of their employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO, disputes that had resulted in a strike; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 by a Thursday in October 1962 (the day of the month is garbled in the text layer); and provided that upon submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the continuing-existence sentence means the order's own text does not end the Board at the report. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so none is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation. The text layer of this order is badly garbled in places, so this description is a paraphrase of the legible words and no part of it is quoted.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 9695, the issue of October 2, 1962) is Executive Order 11054, dated October 1, 1962; its title (a board of inquiry to report on certain labor disputes affecting the maritime industry of the United States) and its text, partly garbled in the text layer, identify it, and it is dated October 1, 1962. The dossier's clause inventory for this order covers unrelated Federal Register rules on neighbouring pages, so I replaced it with the order's own operative text. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the disputes were one-time disputes. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.
